name: umass_cam_action
prose: Precondition: sim and ccb are valid CAM pointers supplied by CAM; sim's softc is either NULL or a valid umass_softc. Postcondition: if the softc is NULL, ccb status is set to CAM_SEL_TIMEOUT and xpt_done is called. Otherwise it switches on ccb_h.func_code. XPT_SCSI_IO: if a transfer is already in progress the ccb gets CAM_SCSI_BUSY and is completed. Otherwise the status is set to CAM_REQ_INPROG|CAM_SIM_QUEUED and the command is transformed by umass_std_transform. If the transform succeeds, quirk-driven INQUIRY (emulated serial-number VPD page, EVPD rejection, fake inquiry data), PREVENT_ALLOW, SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE and START_STOP_UNIT commands are completed immediately via xpt_done, either as CAM_REQ_CMP with SCSI_STATUS_OK or as an illegal request (check condition, devq frozen). Otherwise FORCE_SHORT_INQUIRY may shorten dxfer_len and umass_command_start is called with umass_cam_cb as callback, so the ccb is completed later. If the transform fails, this function does not complete the ccb itself. XPT_PATH_INQ fills in the path inquiry data (transfer speed by quirk or USB speed, max_lun) and completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_RESET_DEV calls umass_reset and completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_GET_TRAN_SETTINGS fills in the SCSI/USB transport settings and completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_SET_TRAN_SETTINGS completes with CAM_FUNC_NOTAVAIL. XPT_CALC_GEOMETRY calls cam_calc_geometry and completes. XPT_NOOP completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. Any other func_code completes with CAM_FUNC_NOTAVAIL. Returns nothing.
note: Placeholder name; the real containing function is umass_cam_action. [sonnet-5-5]

name: r_gestures
prose: Precondition: tp points to a valid touchpad state with hw caps and info configured, time points to a valid timestamp, and ms points to a mouse status that may be modified. Postcondition: if the pressure is high enough (z >= min_pressure_hi, or a finger is already down and z >= min_pressure_lo), it ignores a palm single-touch packet (returns GEST_IGNORE without further changes), otherwise clamps coordinates to the margins, starts a new action if none was in progress, records the position and finger count, maps clickpad softbuttons, adds the tap-hold button, updates the peak pressure, finger count and virtual-scroll state, and returns GEST_IGNORE on a finger-count change, GEST_VSCROLL or GEST_HSCROLL for vertical or horizontal scrolling, GEST_IGNORE (more than one finger) or GEST_ACCUMULATE (one finger) while within the tap timeout, else GEST_MOVE. When the pressure is too low, it clears BUTTON1 on clickpads with softbuttons, resets prev_nfingers, and ends any action in progress: a qualifying tap (no vscroll, zmax >= tap_threshold, within the tap timeout) either completes a double tap (clears in_taphold, sets fingerdown, idletimeout = 0) or starts tap-hold (sets in_taphold, idletimeout, a new taptimeout, the tap_button chosen by finger count 3/2/other, and ORs it into ms->button), while a non-tap clears in_taphold. With no action in progress and in_taphold set, it keeps the tap button pressed until the tap timeout passes and then clears in_taphold. The low-pressure path always returns GEST_IGNORE.

name: vm86_emulate
prose: Precondition: vmf points to a valid vm86 trap frame for the current thread, whose faulting instruction bytes at cs:ip can be read with vm86_fubyte. Postcondition: returns SIGBUS if curpcb->pcb_ext is null, or if the opcode is not handled (in VME mode: any opcode other than the operand-size-prefixed PUSHF/POPF, STI, INTn, POPF or IRET; in non-VME mode: any other than CLI, STI, PUSHF, INTn, IRET, POPF or the prefixed PUSHF/POPF), or when a case breaks out of the switch (VME INTn; VME prefixed POPF, POPF or IRET with VIF set and VIP pending; non-VME STI, POPF, IRET or prefixed POPF with VIP pending; non-VME INTn whose vector is set in the intmap). In VME mode, STI sets VIF and advances IP, then returns SIGKILL after printing 'fatal sti' if VIP is clear, else SIGBUS. Otherwise the instruction is emulated: the stack, flags, VIF and IP/CS are updated in the frame or vm86 state, and the function returns retcode, which is SIGTRAP if PSL_T was set in vmf_eflags on entry, else 0. No locks or references are taken or released.

name: LcpDecodeConfig
prose: Precondition: fp is an LCP fsm, cp..end is a buffer of received LCP configuration options, mode_type is MODE_REQ, MODE_NAK, MODE_REJ or MODE_NOP, and dec is a valid decode context; for a callback option in a REQ, p (the physical link) must be non-NULL. Postcondition: returns nothing; it reads options until the buffer is exhausted or fsm_readopt returns NULL. Each option is handled according to its type and mode_type: in REQ mode it is normally answered with fsm_ack, fsm_nak or fsm_rej (unknown options are rejected), and my_reject is set for rejected options. In NAK/REJ mode the want_*/his_* fields of lcp are updated and his_reject bits are set, and fsm_Close is called when a required callback is NAKed or rejected. After the loop, unless mode_type is MODE_NOP, a REQ on a direct physical link that requires callback but received no callback option gets a callback NAK. A REQ with no MRU option may get an MRU NAK when the limited MRU is below DEF_MRU, which sets his_mru and mru_req. Finally fsm_opt_normalise(dec) is called. A matching magic number in a REQ makes the function sleep in sigsuspend.

name: physical_Open
prose: Precondition: p points to a valid struct physical whose fd is either negative (closed) or an already open descriptor, and whose device list, type and handler fields are initialised. Postcondition: returns p->fd; if fd was already >= 0 it only logs a debug message and returns it unchanged. For PHYS_DIRECT with fd closed it sets the device name to "", uses STDIN_FILENO as fd, tries each device creator while handler is NULL and fd >= 0, closes STDOUT_FILENO, and if fd is still >= 0 sets up the "unknown" stack when no handler was found and calls physical_Found; the result may be a negative fd if a creator closed it. Otherwise it tries each configured device in the list in order while fd < 0: sets the device name, takes the lock, opens a '/'-path with ID0open (O_RDWR|O_NONBLOCK), and runs the device creators while handler is NULL (stopping early if a creator failed but changed fd); if fd is still negative it logs a warning when all creators were tried and unlocks, else it calls physical_Found. Unlock failure paths simply move to the next device. The returned fd may be negative if no device could be opened, and p->handler may remain NULL on success when no creator matched an opened '/' device.
note: Return is p->fd, a struct field, so no formal contract; prose corrected to describe the actual behaviour, including that handler may be NULL on success. [sonnet-5-5]

name: ether_Create
prose: Precondition: p is a valid initialized physical link whose name.full and fd are set (fd < 0 with a name of the form "PPPoE:<iface>[:<provider>]" selects the PPPoE path, otherwise fd is treated as an already open descriptor). Postcondition: on the PPPoE path it decrements p->fd, loads the netgraph modules, creates a netgraph socket node and a PPPoE connection, and on success sets the descriptor callbacks and returns a newly allocated ether device with carrier pending; if malloc fails it returns NULL, if socket node creation fails it frees the device, sets p->fd to -2 and returns NULL, and on any later netgraph failure it returns the result of ether_Abandon(dev, p). On the other path, if p->fd is a netgraph socket it returns a newly allocated device with carrier OK, no hook and slot taken from the SESSIONID environment variable (hex, else 0), returns NULL if allocation fails, and if getsockname fails it closes p->fd, sets it to -1 and returns NULL; if p->fd is not a netgraph socket it returns NULL. When a device is returned, the physical stack is set up with PHYSICAL_FORCE_SYNCNOACF and the caller owns the device.

name: ng_pptpgre_rcvdata_lower
prose: Precondition: hook is a node's lower (IP/GRE) hook and item carries an mbuf whose data starts with an IP header; no session lock is held by the caller. Postcondition: the item is always consumed. Returns EINVAL for runt packets, bad GRE length or bits, unknown, unhooked or disabled session (bad CID), and for late or duplicate sequence numbers (including a duplicate already in the reorder queue). Returns ENOBUFS if m_pullup fails (the item's mbuf is set to NULL, then the item is freed). Returns 0 for a lone ack with no data. For a data packet: in-order packets, and packets that become deliverable after the reorder queue is drained, are acked and delivered through ng_pptpgre_sendq (the session lock is dropped by ng_pptpgre_ack); early packets are queued in the reorder queue (up to reorder_max) with the lock released, and the function returns 0. When the queue is full, the queue head is moved to the send queue to make room. Every other path returns a pointer to result with value 1: access denied (also svcerr_auth AUTH_BADCRED), domain lookup failure, user not found or database error, bad old password, invalid arguments (also svcerr_decode), pw_init/pw_lock/pw_tmp/pw_copy failure, the first rename failure, or pw_mkdb/second rename failure (original file restored from .hold), and fork failure (passfile unlinked and original restored). In the forked child, if exec fails, it unlinks passfile, restores the original from .hold and exits with status 1. The function sets the global passfile and may modify the global yp_password.

name: read_mtree_keywords
prose: Precondition: fp is an open stream positioned at the keywords of an mtree spec line, and node is a valid fsnode whose inode (and its stat) is valid. After the loop it returns that nonzero error if any. Otherwise it sets the file type in st_mode, applies the default timestamp if present, and returns 0 for global defaults (node->name NULL). It also returns 0 after printing a diagnostic when link and contents are both given, a link type lacks a link keyword, the file type mismatches the keywords, or the contents file cannot be stat'ed (freeing the resolved name). If mtree_resolve fails it returns errno. Otherwise it may merge hardlinked inodes (freeing node->inode and bumping the link count), replaces node->contents with the resolved path (freeing the old one), sets st_size from the contents file, and returns 0.

If a device exists at the end, it copies baseexecdevice into it, calls physical_SetupStack, warns if carrier necessity is not CD_DEFAULT, and returns a pointer to the embedded struct device; otherwise it returns NULL. The caller owns the returned device. In the fork-failure case the device is not freed, yet it is still returned.

name: pmc_syscall_handler
prose: Precondition: td is the current thread and syscall_args points to a pmc_syscall_args giving the operation code and user data pointer. Postcondition: returns 0 on success, otherwise an errno, and bumps the syscall and syscall-error counters. The pmc_sx lock is taken exclusive (or downgraded to shared by some ops) and released before return. If pmc_hook is NULL it returns EINVAL at once; if the exclusive lock cannot be taken it returns ENOSYS. For the PMC_OP_PMCADMIN case, the caller needs PRIV_PMC_MANAGE (otherwise the priv_check error is returned) and the user pmcadmin struct must be copyable in (otherwise the copyin error is returned). EINVAL is returned if the cpu is out of range, the state is neither DISABLED nor FREE, or the row index is out of range; ENXIO if the cpu is inactive; EBUSY if disabling a thread-disposition row, or if a PMC is allocated on that hardware slot. Otherwise, with the thread bound to that cpu, DISABLED clears the enabled flag and marks the row standalone if it was enabled, and FREE sets the flag and unmarks the row if it was disabled; other cases are no-ops. The PMCALLOCATE, PMCATTACH, PMCDETACH, PMCGETMSR and PMCRELEASE cases are other branches of the same function. PMCALLOCATE copies the struct in, calls pmc_do_op_pmcallocate, and copies it back out on success. PMCGETMSR returns EINVAL for a non-virtual, inherited, or not exactly owner-attached PMC, and ENOSYS if the class has no get_msr. Otherwise it copies out the MSR, flags the owner process with PMC_PP_ENABLE_MSR_ACCESS and forces a context switch. PMCRELEASE copies in the id and calls pmc_do_op_pmcrelease.

Postcondition: returns nothing; for each of the cy rows starting at y it writes zero bytes to the window with set/reset programmed to val, so the pixels from x to x+cx are set to val, using partial-byte masks at unaligned edges and moving the window origin across banks as needed; at the end it sets the GDC bit mask to 0xff, set/reset to 0 and set/reset enable to 0, but it does not restore the read/write mode (0x0005) or the data rotate/function select (0x0003) set at the start.

Postcondition: returns 0 on success, with the taskqueue started, PCI/BAR memory and the MSI-X interrupt mapped and set up, the device family and firmware names chosen from the PCI product id, the ctxt_info, ICT (and on AX210+ prph_scratch and prph_info) DMA buffers, all TX rings and the RX ring allocated, the net80211 capabilities filled in, the rxba data and watchdog callout initialised, and the config_intrhook preinit hook established. Returns ENXIO on any failure: taskqueue start failure, missing PCIe capability, no MSI-X, BAR or IRQ allocation failure, interrupt setup failure, unknown adapter type or an unsupported AX201 hw rev, or a DMA, ring or intrhook failure. Failures in the DMA, ring or intrhook steps free the DMA buffers and rings allocated by this call, but the earlier failure returns (taskqueue, BAR, IRQ, interrupt setup) release nothing they had acquired. On the intrhook failure path the ICT buffer is freed only if its vaddr is non-NULL. A failure of the first DMA allocation (ctxt_info_dma) returns directly without cleanup.

name: cas_attach

Postcondition: allocates the ifnet, creates the taskqueue, resets the chip, creates the DMA tags, allocates and loads the control data, creates the TX maps, and allocates and loads the RX buffers. It then attaches a PHY through MII (external, internal fallback, or SERDES), registers the interface with ether_ifattach and sets its capabilities, and returns 0. On any failure (taskqueue start, DMA tag creation, DMA alloc/load/create, or PHY attach, which gives ENXIO or the mii_attach error) it releases everything acquired so far in reverse order, frees the taskqueue and ifnet, and returns the nonzero errno. A load that succeeds but leaves the DMA address 0 can return 0 from the failure path since error is 0.

name: ahc_handle_scsiint
prose: Precondition: ahc is a valid controller softc whose sequencer is paused because a SCSI interrupt is pending (intstat is passed but not used). Postcondition: returns nothing; it reads SSTAT0/SSTAT1 (on a twin-channel controller it may toggle SBLKCTL SELBUSB to the other channel), and if no cause is found it prints a spurious-interrupt message, clears CLRSCSIINT, unpauses and returns. Otherwise it clears the critical section and handles exactly one cause, in priority order: (1) Ultra2 transceiver IOERR, which resets the channel; (2) SCSIRSTI, which resets the channel without initiating a reset; (3) SCSIPERR, which logs the parity error, queues or flags a parity-error message, forces renegotiation, clears CLRSCSIINT and unpauses; (4) SELTO, which stops the selection, clears message state and interrupt state, completes the waiting SCB with CAM_SEL_TIMEOUT via device reset handling (or dumps card state if the SCB lookup fails), clears CLRSCSIINT and restarts the sequencer; (5) BUSFREE with ENBUSFREE enabled, which handles the expected or unexpected bus free (abort, bus device reset, PPR/WDTR/SDTR rejection requeue, or CAM_UNEXP_BUSFREE aborts with diagnostics), clears CLRSCSIINT and restarts the sequencer; (6) otherwise it prints a missing-case message and clears CLRSCSIINT. In the P_MESGOUT abort cases it dereferences scb, which may be NULL if the connection was not identified.

Postcondition: returns nothing; the command is dispatched in one of these ways. If the device is offline, pCmd->Result is RETURN_BAD_DEVICE and completion is called. If the LBA range exceeds the device capacity, or the command is not READ/WRITE/VERIFY, Result is RETURN_INVALID_REQUEST and completion is called. For READ/WRITE with device mode below 8, or with no usable physical SG, DMA is disabled and the queue flushed, and the data is transferred by PIO. Result is then RETURN_SUCCESS, RETURN_NEED_LOGICAL_SG, RETURN_INVALID_REQUEST (size not a multiple of 512) or RETURN_IDE_ERROR. DMA is re-enabled and completion is called. For UDMA, a PRD table is allocated, or Result is RETURN_DEVICE_BUSY and completion is called if allocation fails. The PRD table is filled from the SG list and the command is queued with mvSataQueueCommand. On queue failure Result is RETURN_IDE_ERROR (or RETURN_DEVICE_BUSY if the queue is full), the PRD table is freed and completion is called. On the UDMA path pDevice->QueueLength is incremented after the queue attempt, even after a failure. For VERIFY, a non-UDMA verify command (EXT if lba48) is queued, and on queue failure the same queue_failed handling runs with no PRD table to free. On success the completion callback is invoked later.
note: Placeholder name; the slice is the tail of fDeviceSendCommand. [sonnet-5-5]

name: bxe_tx_encap
prose: Precondition: fp is a valid fastpath and *m_head is a valid mbuf chain with a packet header, to be transmitted on the TX ring at the current producer indexes. Postcondition: it returns 0 on success, after the mbuf is DMA-mapped and stored in the tx_mbuf_chain slot, the start BD, parsing BD and data BDs are written, the producer indexes advance, the doorbell is rung and tx_pkts is incremented. name: zio_ddt_write
prose: Precondition: zio is a dedup write (BP_GET_DEDUP(bp) set, checksum matching zp_checksum, bp either a hole or the io_bp_override) and is not a Direct I/O write. Postcondition: it always returns zio itself, with the DDT lock taken by ddt_enter released again and any dde_io lock it took released. There are five outcomes. If ddt_lookup returns no entry (DDT over quota), dedup is turned off in zp and bp, and io_pipeline is set to ZIO_WRITE_PIPELINE unless there is a bp override. If dedup verify finds a collision, a weak checksum is upgraded to the spa dedup checksum (transforms popped, stage reset to OPEN, bp zeroed), otherwise dedup is turned off in zp and bp; either way io_pipeline is set to ZIO_WRITE_PIPELINE. If the entry has enough DVAs or an in-flight write will provide them, the bp is filled from the entry (for a brand-new override entry the entry is extended from the override bp), and the entry refcount is incremented, except that a rewrite whose refilled bp equals io_bp_orig sets ZIO_FLAG_NOPWRITE and skips the refcount increment. When there is an in-flight lead write that suffices, zio is added as a parent of that lead zio. If the entry is ganged and more DVAs are needed, dedup is turned off and io_pipeline is set to ZIO_WRITE_PIPELINE. Otherwise a child write for the DVA shortfall is created with copies reduced if the entry already has DVAs or a write is pending, zio is its parent, the child becomes the lead zio for the entry (allocating dde_io and saving the original phys if needed, chaining any previous lead as its child), the refcount is incremented, and the child is dispatched with zio_nowait.

name: parse_rx_slots
prose: Precondition: state is a valid initialised VCHIQ state whose remote shared state is mapped, and the caller is the slot handler that owns the rx side; no service reference is held on entry. Postcondition: returns nothing; processes each message from state->rx_pos up to the remote tx_pos snapshot, dispatching by message type (open, openack, close, data, connect, bulk, bulk done, padding, pause, resume, remote use/release and invalid ids), taking and releasing a service reference per message where one is looked up. After a message is handled, or skipped because no service matched, it advances rx_pos by calc_stride(size) and releases the slot when the end of a slot is reached. If parse_open, a close or data callback, a bulk mutex lock, or the queue_message in PAUSE handling fails with RETRY or interruption, it jumps to bail_not_ready, stops without advancing rx_pos past the current message, and drops any held service reference so the message can be retried later.

Postcondition: it hashes the tuple, and returns NULL immediately if a key's by-reference data cannot be loaded (dtrace_canload fails) or a CPU fault flag is set. Otherwise it copies the keys and key data into the chunk, publishes it at the head of the hash chain and returns the new dvar. If publishing fails the chunk goes to the dirty list and the whole operation retries.

It also returns early if the processor private-resource check fails, comparing (UINT8)(Length - fixed size) with (UINT8)(count*4) and printing "Invalid private resource number". Postcondition: returns 0 if vprsactx is NULL; returns 1 without changes if params is empty; otherwise it first applies the four FIPS indicator parameters (returning 0 if any fails), then parses digest, properties, pad mode, PSS saltlen, MGF1 digest and MGF1 properties into local state, returning 0 (usually with an error raised) on any invalid value: wrong data type, a bad or disallowed padding mode (OAEP, PSS without sign/verify operation, PKCS1/none/X9.31 unless the key is a plain RSA key, plus the FIPS-only X9.31 key-size and permission checks), saltlen given without PSS padding, saltlen below RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_AUTO_DIGEST_MAX, restricted-key violations (autodetected saltlen on non-verify, saltlen below min_saltlen), or MGF1 digest given without PSS padding. Only after all parsing succeeds does it store pad_mode and saltlen into the context; if no md is set, no digest was given and padding is PSS it defaults the digest name to RSA_DEFAULT_DIGEST_NAME; it then sets up the MGF1 digest if given and the digest (or, if no digest name, checks padding against the current mdnid), returning 0 if any of these fails, else 1. On a late failure pad_mode and saltlen have already been updated, and FIPS indicator settings may have been changed by earlier steps. The caller keeps ownership of everything it passed in.

On failure (GSS_S_NO_CRED when no usable acceptor cred or mech not allowed by default, GSS_S_BAD_MECH when the mech or its accept routine is missing, GSS_S_FAILURE on allocation failure, or the mechanism or name-conversion status, with the minor status mapped) it releases any temporary source name, sets *src_name to GSS_C_NO_NAME if src_name is non-NULL, and, if *context_handle was GSS_C_NO_CONTEXT, frees the newly created union context (deleting the internal mech context when possible); a pre-existing context is kept for the caller to delete. name: _gssapi_unwrap_cfx_iov
prose: Precondition: minor_status is writable, ctx is a valid Kerberos GSS context with a crypto handle, iov points to iov_count buffer descriptors that should contain a HEADER buffer (plus optional PADDING, TRAILER, DATA and SIGN_ONLY buffers) holding a CFX wrap token, and conf_state and qop_state may be NULL or writable. Postcondition: *minor_status is first set to 0. Early returns, with no buffer release: GSS_S_FAILURE with EINVAL if there is no header buffer or if the padding buffer is non-empty; GSS_S_DEFECTIVE_TOKEN if the header is shorter than a token, if the token ID, flags (acceptor flag, acceptor-subkey flag) or filler are wrong; whatever _gk_verify_buffers returns if it is not GSS_S_COMPLETE; GSS_S_UNSEQ_TOKEN with ERANGE if the high 32 bits of the sequence number are nonzero; or the nonzero code from the message-order check with *minor_status 0 (the context mutex is held only around that check). *conf_state, if non-NULL, is set to 1 if the sealed flag is set and 0 otherwise once the flags are validated. After that, a calloc failure gives GSS_S_FAILURE with ENOMEM. Otherwise the sealed or unsealed path checks RRC, EC and buffer lengths and either decrypts the data in place (sealed) or verifies the checksum (unsealed). Failures here are GSS_S_DEFECTIVE_TOKEN for bad lengths or RRC, the error from unrotate_iov, GSS_S_FAILURE with a Kerberos error or EINVAL (unsealed bad RRC), and GSS_S_BAD_MIC if the decrypted header differs from the token. Every failure after the allocation attempt frees the temporary array and calls gss_release_iov_buffer on iov, which releases the caller's buffers that the GSS layer allocated. On success it sets *qop_state (if non-NULL) to GSS_C_QOP_DEFAULT, frees the temporary array, sets *minor_status to 0 and returns GSS_S_COMPLETE. In the unsealed path the header token's EC and RRC fields are zeroed in place.

prose: Precondition: argv holds argc valid C strings, with an optional leading "-s" flag (selecting the short key generation path) followed by an optional decimal RSA key size. name: mi_listener
prose: Precondition: conn is a valid listener address string, smfi points to a valid filter description, and L_Mutex is usable (it is initialised elsewhere, before the loop locks it). Postcondition: returns MI_FAILURE immediately if mi_opensocket() fails (or, with workers pool, if mi_pool_controller_init() fails), without destroying the mutex. Transient accept, select and fd-range errors are retried. The function breaks out with MI_FAILURE when listenfd is invalid, when select fails MAX_FAILS_S times, when select reports an exception on the socket, or when accept, malloc or session creation fail MAX_FAILS_A, MAX_FAILS_M or MAX_FAILS_T times in a row; on a failed malloc or session creation the accepted socket is closed and the context freed. After the loop, on MI_FAILURE it calls mi_stop_milters(MILTER_ABRT); on success it logs if the stop was not MILTER_CONT and calls mi_closener(). It then destroys L_Mutex and returns MI_SUCCESS or MI_FAILURE.

name: hpgps_receive
prose: Precondition: rbufp->recv_peer is a valid peer whose procptr is a refclockproc and whose unitptr is an initialised hpgpsunit. Postcondition: returns nothing. An empty reply returns at once. While up->linecnt > 0 the line is appended to the status screen buffer when it fits, the buffer is logged to clockstats when linecnt reaches 0, and the function returns. Otherwise the line is logged, lastrec is set, pollcnt is set to 2 and the status buffer is reset. If the prompt shows an error, "*CLS" is written, and CEVNT_FAULT is reported if the write is short. A timezone reply (+/-) sets up->tzhour and up->tzminute, or reports CEVNT_BADREPLY if it is malformed or out of range. A malformed or unrecognised timecode reply or a bad checksum reports CEVNT_BADREPLY. An invalid date, or an unrecognised leap indicator, or a refclock_process failure reports CEVNT_BADTIME. In each of these cases it returns without further processing. Note that pp->year, hour, minute and second are written by sscanf before validation. A valid timecode gets timezone-corrected time fields and day, and sets pp->leap from the sync and leap characters (leap announcements only count in June or December). It then calls refclock_process, sets lastref and calls refclock_receive. If CLK_FLAG4 is set, it sets linecnt to 22 and writes ":SYSTEM:PRINT?", reporting CEVNT_FAULT if the write is short.
note: The full function is annotated; the earlier drop was wrong because the slice is a fragment of hpgps_receive. [sonnet-5-5]

name: clock_select
prose: Precondition: the association list peer_list and the global system state (sys_peer, sys_reftime, sys_epoch, sys_minclock, sys_maxclock, sys_minsane, sys_orphan and others) are initialised, and the caller is the NTP protocol code that runs the selection. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it reallocates its static endpoint/peer/index work arrays and sets every peer's new_status (reject, sane, candidate, excess, sync candidate, system peer or PPS) by culling unfit, orphan-excluded and falsetickers, then voting out outliers by selection jitter. It also sets sys_survivors, leap_vote_ins/del, sys_clockhop and, when a system peer is chosen, sys_offset/sys_jitter. If no system peer is chosen it sets orphwait and reports EVNT_NOPEER when a previous system peer existed, sets sys_peer to NULL, copies new_status into status for all peers and returns. If the chosen peer's epoch is not newer than sys_epoch it returns early without copying statuses or updating the clock. Otherwise it reports PEVNT_NEWPEER if the system peer changed, copies new_status into status for all peers and calls clock_update on the chosen peer.

name: SM_STATE(WPA_PTK, PTKCALCNEGOTIATING)
prose: Precondition: sm is a WPA authenticator state machine whose last_rx_eapol_key holds a received EAPOL-Key msg 2/4 with length fields already validated, and sm->wpa_auth is valid. Postcondition: the function returns void and always clears EAPOLKeyReceived and update_snonce. It tries to derive the PTK, with the PMK or each PSK, the OWE SHA256 workaround and the no-KDK workaround, until the frame's MIC verifies (or AEAD decrypts for FILS). If no PTK verifies it either asks the RADIUS server for the PSK and sets waiting_radius_psk, or logs an invalid MIC, reports a PSK failure if a PSK was found, and leaves the PTK unchanged.
